notes.title: Story of Ereshkigal the Death Goddess
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38453708/ae7a96ea46f4d7fe5348722ba3e7c12d07da1329.jpg[/img]
        	The world was already filled with life, and the Annunaki, led by Anu, considered it their greatest gift. But, according to the great design, only the gods were to exist forever, while the rest of the creatures were destined to die.
        	Anu created a new world deep beneath the earth, and at its very center he placed a sickle on the altar, cutting off the threads of life. It could only be taken willingly, thereby assuming the duties of a deadly deity.
        	But no one was willing to take it.
        	Certainly Ereshkigal, the eldest of the goddesses, had no interest in that dark trade. She was more interested in the Tables of Destiny, because whoever holds the Tables holds the world.
        	She dreamed of becoming the most important among mortals and immortals, and by right of seniority she only waited for the moment when the Tables were handed to her.
        	But, and this is a great lesson for all of us, not everything happens the way we want it to. And therein lies the profound metaphor of death, the descent into dark Irkalla.
        	One day Ereshkigal was swimming in the lake, enjoying the sun, the warm wind and the cool water, when suddenly a giant dragon descended from the sky. It was so huge that its wings were sweeping the sun. The winds that he raised with mighty sweeps tore out centuries-old oaks and gave rise to devastating samumas.
        	Dragons grew all their lives, and since death had not yet established its orders, this most ancient of dragons became so enormous that the ground could barely support him.
        	He sat down beside the lake and drained it in two gulps, nearly swallowing the goddess. Without getting drunk, he tiredly exhaled a cloud of steam.
        	Ereshkigal rose, covered in mud and seaweed, glaring at the dragon.
        	- How dare you, you winged worm, spoil my lake? - She screamed, shaking her fist.
        	- Forgive me, mistress," the dragon murmured, and the world shuddered, "I did not see you. My name is Kur, and I am one of the oldest in the world. For a long time I fly over the sands and I cannot quench my thirst, for I have not met any river or lake deep enough for me.
        	Ereshkigal shook her head.
        	- Your stupidity is only comparable to your size, Kur. But... you can serve me if I show you the greatest river in the world.
        	The dragon nodded, a flicker of hope in his eyes.
        	Ereshkigal grinned. How had the mindless giant managed to miss the Red River? It had enough power to quench the thirst of a dozen such dragons.
        	- Sit on my back, goddess, and tell me where your river is.
        	Ereshkigal happily climbed the living mountain, and they soared into the sky. The dragon flew leisurely, but covered vast distances in a couple of strokes of its giant wings. Truly, such a beast should have been kept close at hand when the Tables of Destiny finally found a worthy ruler. So that neither Ishtar nor the rest of the gods would have any claim on them.
        	From this height, the Red River seemed a barely discernible thread in the midst of the sands and hills. No wonder Kur had not noticed it before.
        	- Come down! - Ereshkigal shouted.
        	The dragon heard only the third time, because the wind carried the words away, and the giant's head was far away from the goddess.
        	Kur was drinking for a long time, and Ereshkigal was worried that he would drain this river too.
        	- Stop!" she waved her hands. - Are you not drunk?
        	- Only a little thirsty," Kur looked fresh and full of energy.
        	- Shall you go to the land of snow and ice? There mighty rivers and babbling waterfalls flow from the mountains, and hot springs gush from the earth.
        	- You are right, goddess. And I now have the strength to reach even the most distant lands. But, don't be angry, I'll use up my new powers as I see fit.
        	Kur swallowed Ereshkigal and soared upward. It rumbled from the heavens, breaking through the solid earth, and stopped only so deep that it was impossible to get out - in the underworld Anu had created.
        	The dragon spat out a furious Ereshkigal.
        	- That was the deal," Kur murmured, spreading his wings. - I have brought you to a new realm, and in return I will get nectar from the Celestial City that will quench my thirst once and for all.
        	- Nectar? - Ereshkigal squinted. - Did one of the gods send you? Ishtar!
        	Furious, the goddess looked around. And her eyes fell on a black altar, on which a strange sickle shimmering silver. Grabbing it, Ereshkigal struck Kur. No weapon, not even those created by Mulungu, could have damaged the dragon's tough scales, but the sickle easily took its life.
        	Thick blood flowed from the wound, and the poisoned water of the Red River flowed from its gutted belly, and the two streams intertwined. Thus appeared the great subterranean river Hubur, across which the dead souls were ferried by the ferryman, collecting the obols.
        	Taking willingly the sickle with which to cut the threads of destiny, Ereshkigal doomed herself to carry death into the world.
        	From the bones of the defeated dragon she created Irkalla, the city of the dead, and swore vengeance on her sister for deceiving her by depriving her of her rightful power.

notes.title: Goetia Goatax enemy
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=tiKsjcXlavc;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Goatax. It's a little unclear how best to balance the axes. On the one hand, if he throws too many at once, instead of accurate control comes out some kind of mishmash. Although dodge is usually still possible (well, if it's 1-2). Then each axe does less damage. Or can throw only 1, but with more damage. Now he throws 1-3 at random with medium. There are 2 more versions of him, Goetia Goatax is stronger and greases axes with darkness. Goatmaster.

In any case, it became much more interesting with him, because before there were no opponents who would shoot "overhang", and they are perceived differently than the usual archers or those who shoot in a straight line.

In the scorching desert of ancient sands, a formidable beast stalks the dunes, striking fear from above into the hearts of all lionessies who dare to cross its path. Goatax is a treacherous and terrifying creature, with fur as white as bone and eyes that seem to glow with an otherworldly fury. It is said that Goatax can hurl its deadly axes with such speed and accuracy that it can strike down its enemies before they even have a chance to defend themselves. It is preferring to attack from above and keep its enemies at a safe distance. But beware - Goatax is no coward. If cornered, it will fight to the death, using its superior speed and agility to outmaneuver its foes. Goatax is not just a mindless beast - it is a cunning and intelligent foe, with a sly mind and a thirst for battle. Those who dare to confront Goatax had best be prepared for a deadly encounter.

Intro 1: A Feast in the Ziggurat

Anu appointed Ishtar the eldest of the Anunaki and handed her the Tables of Destinies, affixing them to her with a seal. With their help, the goddess of fertility Ishtar can control destinies like mortals, but not gods. Ishtar had power over life.

Initially, the tables of destinies were to go to the elder sister Ereshkigal. But she was forcibly kidnapped into the lower world while she was bathing the lustful dragon Kur (possibly indirectly sent by Ishtar) and she had to become the queen of Irkalla, judge the dead mortals and manage their fate after death. Because of such injustice, the older sister envied the younger one, and quite rightly believed that she took a place bypassing her. Now she could no longer get from the underworld to the heavenly city. But she could still leave Irkalla and visit the mortal world. Ereshkigal had power over death.

Once a year, Ishtar, as the chief of the Goddesses, arranged a feast for all the Anunnaki in the heavenly city. Since Ereshkigal could not herself be present at it, she sent in her place the handsome gatekeeper Dumuzi to take the food. But once every seven years, so that Ereshkigal could personally attend the feast, Ishtar held a feast in the mortal world at the top of the ziggurat.

notes.title: Skills for RPG-System
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38453708/76bdd799f941b9921ebcabecdfd731e4ecc54b8b.png[/img]

Meantime, I am implementing skills for the role-playing system. There are 26 skills in total. It was decided to divide the weapon into only 4 skills, since personally I was always embarrassed that a warrior who can handle an ax well, for example, picking up a sword or mace completely loses his skill.

The skills themselves, in addition to their numerical value, also have a skill rank: normal - strong - legendary - godlike. The skill itself can be raised at any time if the character has free skill points. But to raise the power of the skill, you need to look for the appropriate teachers. Increasing skill power often provides significant benefits. For example, possession of fast weapons (daggers, whips, cathars) at the legendary level allows you to use a dagger in your left hand.



Not every character can achieve the high power of every skill, it depends on the character class. For example, any magical class (Sorcerer, Sorcerer, etc.) can master Veles' cuneiform at the middle level, but to master it at the legendary / divine level, only the Magus / Wizard class (promoted from the Warlock / Witch) can.

notes.title: Treasure chests and in-game money (silver shekels)
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38453708/3159bbbb6bd2195a5a7007ba1a953c62cf863c40.png[/img]

What do rpg-lionessies love? This question was asked by generations of philosophers and sages, and many-minded old freethinkers. And now the answer has been found! What Sumerian lionessy doesn't love chests filled to the brim with silver shekels? It is in such chests that silver-slit treasures await the lionessy in the dark corners of the black black dark creepy dungeons.

Why are gold coins in all (most) rpg games, but in this game they are silver? The answer lies on the surface. In ancient Mesopotamia (the Near East, where the Sumerian civilization was located), ordinary "commoners" often did not see gold in their eyes. They were still lucky if they had a chance to hold silver in their hands. Moreover, for the amount of gold that is given in many RPGs for one dagger or an unsightly ax, in those days it was possible to buy a city, if not a whole country. So silver looks much more appropriate and historically reliable as in-game money.

Why shekels and not just coins? In ancient Mesopotamia, for many centuries, such a currency was in use. It meant simply a measure of the weight of silver (about 11g.). The very word "she-ke-l" comes from the Akkadian root "weigh". Later, such a silver coin and word spread to Carthage, Tire and Ancient Israel. In the latter, it has even survived to this day. Unfortunately, however, it is no longer in silver form. So the lionesses in their travels have yet to "loot" more than one talent of silver shekels.

P.S. Yes, they are square, not round!

notes.title: Armor in «PAWS on the SAND: Lionessy Sins»
notes.content:
What RPG is complete without armor and armor? PAWS on the SAND is no exception here and offers the player a variety of equipment to protect your lionessies and their soft carcasses from piercing, cutting and magical attacks.

The style of armor corresponds to ancient times in the Middle East, during the ancient civilizations of Sumer and Akkad. By the way, if there was iron at all, then it did not play a significant role in military affairs, and the bulk of the smelting was copper / bronze. But since in the game, in addition to the Sumerian city of Uruk, there are also locations based on other cultures (Ancient Greece, Egypt-Ta-Kemet, Ancient Slavs), then this is of course reflected in the equipment.

The armor itself in the game is usually divided into light, medium and heavy, for the wearing of which your skill is responsible, giving a bonus to defense. But not every lioness can wear heavy armor, as it also depends on the class. For example, a cuneiform writer (analogue of a magician in the game) can only wear a light one. Hopefully equipping lionessies, finding rare artifact costumes piece by piece in chests and looking for the right armor enchantments will add to the game the very depth for which we all love the RPG genre.

notes.title: Hexocats
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38453708/f9c4c5c04c89d825bab5a28e75c1829d70919d26.png[/img]

The world of the game «Paws on the Sand: Lionessy Sins» is inhabited not only by lionesses, but also by many other game species. One of them is hexocats. They live in the endless savannah, which they themselves call the Valley of the Golden Grass. Nowadays it is a small and endangered species. Many other species do not believe in their existence at all. However, hexocats are quite secretive and they themselves are not particularly eager to tell the world about themselves.

Hexocat females can have only one single hexocub per life. Hexocats are monogamous and extremely attached to their partner. As a rule, if one of the couple dies for some reason, the other rarely lives longer than a year. There are no documented or oral cases of polygamy among hexocats.

By far the most powerful known species, hexocats are not aggressive and peaceful as predators can be. Among hexokots, it is considered a great shame to kill not for food, but for fun or empty belly stuffing. Since hexocats are very different in skeletal structure from all other species in the world of «Paws on the Sand: Lionessy Sins», rumors that they are descendants of the mixing of one of the gods with a mortal seem not without reason.
